acceptanceCriteria: An owner decision accepts or rejects an opt-in goal profile that amends LCP-V0-008; without acceptance the one-continuation rule stays unchanged.
If accepted: continuation is decided only by the claimed ticket's acceptance gate result, never by a model verdict or transcript content, and Stop never runs expensive verification itself.

Hard bounds are enforced and visible: a continuation cap, a no-progress stop after N consecutive unchanged gate results and trees, release on user interruption, and one settlement outcome (COMPLETED, BLOCKED, BUDGET_REACHED) recorded in the ticket's receipts.
body:
Filed 2026-10-22 from a review of openchamber/openchamber (MIT) 'Session Goals'.

OpenChamber turns a prompt into a goal: after each agent turn an independent auditor (a cheap model that sees only the objective and the latest reply) returns continue/done/stuck; it auto-continues, completes with one settlement notification, and stops as BLOCKED only after three consecutive 'stuck' verdicts. Hard stops: token budget, a cap on automatic continuations, and turn errors; an explicit user stop always wins. Per-turn notifications are suppressed while the goal runs.

Corvint today deliberately allows only one bounded remediation continuation at Stop (LCP-V0-008, stop_hook_active releases). The Corvint-shaped version replaces the model auditor with a deterministic one: the claimed ticket's acceptance criteria and required gates (gate run / criterion verification) decide done; the measured signal for 'no progress' is an unchanged gate result plus unchanged committed tree across N consecutive continuations. This also gives lanes a principled bound for the reruns behind V1-1629 (dogfood-change rerun 4-19 times) and V1-1630 (polling loops).

Changing the one-continuation rule is an owner decision; this ticket proposes an explicitly enrolled, opt-in profile, not a default.
title: Tasks goal mode: opt-in bounded continuation until a claimed ticket's acceptance gate passes, with a no-progress stop
